text:
Minnesota had this one with 1:58 to go. Nick Foligno, a fourth-liner playing 11 minutes, scored his second goal of the season (his first since opening night) to make it 3-2, and our win probability had the Wild at 88%. Thirty-five seconds later Marco Rossi, the centre Minnesota sent to Vancouver in the Quinn Hughes trade, tied it, and the Canucks won it in a shootout.

Rossi was the story all night. He scored twice, both to tie the game: a power-play tip in the second period and then the equalizer at 18:37 of the third, the goal that moved Vancouver from a 10% chance to win to 52%. No player added more to his team's win chances. He played 19:30 with Elias Pettersson out of the lineup and the subject of steady trade talk, and Brock Boeser assisted on all three Canucks goals in regulation. Zeev Buium, the other young piece from that trade, scored the 2-2 goal 30 seconds into the third on a shot with a 2% chance.

The process favoured Minnesota. The Wild had 2.80 expected goals (the quality of their chances) to 2.10, with almost all of theirs at even strength, and they controlled the second period 0.97 to 0.37. Matt Boldy and Jared Spurgeon scored in that period, both set up by Kirill Kaprizov. In our replays of every shot the Wild win 63% of the time. Jesper Wallstedt, who came in with a perfect November, gave up 0.9 goals more than his 24 shots deserved.

Leevi Meriläinen made the night's biggest save in overtime, stopping Joel Eriksson Ek on a 28% chance, and then the shootout went Vancouver's way. Maxim Shabanov, Boldy and Kaprizov were all stopped, Kaprizov off the post according to NHL.com's Heather Rule, and Jake DeBrusk scored the only goal of it.

It ends Minnesota's five-game winning streak, though the Wild still picked up a point: by Rule's count they are 11-0-3 in their last 14. For Vancouver, the night belonged to the player who used to wear the other sweater.
headline: Marco Rossi haunts the Wild, Canucks win shootout
